businessProblem: Amtek Auto Ltd. has defaulted on bond repayments of approximately Rs. 800 crore in September 2015. Total group debt stands at approximately Rs. 14,000 crore accumulated through aggressive acquisition-led expansion. Cash generation is weak and insufficient to service debt at current levels. Asset sales are being explored but execution timelines and valuations are uncertain. The core question is whether the acquisition-funded growth model is sustainable and what the highest-priority actions are to avoid a broader creditor crisis.

evidence.finding: Bond default of approximately Rs. 800 crore in September 2015
Total group debt approximately Rs. 14,000 crore as of 2015
Operating cash flows insufficient to service debt at current levels
evidence.source: Financial analysis of cash conversion relative to debt quantum

evidence.finding: Aggressive acquisition-led expansion created multi-entity group structure with cash-management complexity
Automotive sector slowdown reducing volume and pricing support for component manufacturers
Asset sales being explored; valuation and execution timeline uncertain
Management acknowledged need for debt reduction but no confirmed standstill or lender coordination in place
Working-capital pressure compounding debt-service stress in manufacturing operations
